# Temple Scroll Column 39 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 39 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**39:1** You shall make a moat around the temple, outside the outer court, so that no one enters My temple suddenly.

**39:2** The moat shall be one hundred cubits wide and very deep.

**39:3** Between the moat and the outer court there shall be a space of seven cubits; and you shall plant trees in it.

**39:4** You shall make a parapet along the moat so that no one falls into it.

**39:5** They shall not defile My temple by entering it suddenly in their uncleanness.

**39:6** They shall sanctify My temple and fear My sanctuary, for I dwell among them.

**39:7** You shall make latrines outside the temple city, to the northwest, at a distance from the city.

**39:8** They shall go out to them — roofed places with pits within them — into which the filth shall descend.

**39:9** They shall not be visible from the temple city at any distance.

**39:10** No man shall go out to them on the Sabbath; the distance shall be three thousand cubits from the temple city.

**39:11** You shall make three places to the east of the city, separated from one another, for the different types of uncleanness.

**39:12** The places shall be for those with skin diseases, for those with discharges, and for men who have had an emission of seed.

**39:13** They shall not enter the temple city until their purification is complete; on the day of their purification they shall wash and be clean.

**39:14** They shall bring their offerings as prescribed; and the priest shall pronounce them clean.

**39:15** After that they may enter the temple city; no unclean person shall be found in it.

**39:16** For it is the city of the temple; I the LORD have hallowed it and set My name upon it; and it shall be holy forever.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows EMET closely. "Latrines" used by all three translators (PNEUMA initially rendered as "public toilets" but the term "latrines" is appropriately neutral). "Parapet" preferred unanimously over PNEUMA's "railing." "Fear My sanctuary" preserved over LOGOS's "hold in reverence" — yare' is best rendered "fear" in cultic contexts.*
